_comment: Reviewed Semgrep exceptions. Each entry permits EXACTLY ONE finding and
nothing more. An entry matches only when the rule id, the path, the line
and the current sha256 of the file all agree, so an exception cannot
broaden: the same rule firing in another file, another rule firing in this
file, the finding moving, or the file changing at all are each a failure.
An exception that matches no finding is also a failure. A finding that has
gone away must be removed from this file deliberately, not left behind to
The runtime source is digest-governed: tools/capability/package_resolution.py
is an installed Generation-12 object and its digest is authority. Adding an
inline nosemgrep comment would change that digest and break the chain
between the checkout and the installed runtime, which is why the exception
lives here rather than at the call site.

exceptions.justification: 0o700 is owner-only staging-directory mode and is stricter than the rule's 0o644 recommendation; directories require execute permission for traversal. The rule reads the named constant _STAGING_MODE rather than its value, so it cannot see that the mode grants nothing to group or other. The call site is _abandon(), which leaves an unpublished staging tree readable to the operator who owns it and to nobody else.
